title: Early Childhood Studies
award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 30S/45Q to fewer than 60S/90Q units

program.section_heading: EARLY CHILDHOOD STUDIES — Certificate of Achievement in Early Childhood Studies
outcomes: Examine factors affecting child development in family relationships, while demonstrating an understanding of diverse family and cultural groups, their rituals and traditions in the United States of America.

Demonstrate understanding, application, and implementation of Developmentally Appropriate Practices (DAP) in the Early Childhood Environment (ECE) and reporting to agencies as needed within a variety of curriculum philosophies; and development of child and professional portfolios.

Demonstrate the ability to identify and describe typical development, basic needs, major theories, problem areas, and the impact of familial, community, and social influences on a child’ s development.
Illustrate the understanding of biological, psychological, physical, and linguistic development processes of children from conception through adolescence.

Demonstrate knowledge of a variety of observation and assessment methods and tools used to assess children’ s typical and atypical development and behavior; apply assessment data to develop developmentally appropriate classroom and individual curriculum plans, guidance, discipline plans, developmentally appropriate environments, and the development of both child and professional portfolios.

notes: The certificate section begins on page 28 and its MAJOR FIELD table continues at the top of page 29 ('continued on next page'). That table is the first one on page 29, before the Associate in Arts section, and it was read as the certificate's.

The section names no job titles. It says the certificate prepares students for employment in child development programs (preschools, children's centers, family childcare centers, school age programs, infant and toddler programs). These are settings rather than careers, so careers is left empty; a reviewer may wish to check.
The text mentions an additional six to nine units for options in a particular area, but lists no courses or option blocks for them.
Outcomes are copied as printed, including the PDF spacing in 'child’ s' and 'children’ s'.
